title: Poll vSAN Data Protection snapshot tasks to a terminal state
prompt:
Fix the asynchronous snapshot workflow in src/vsan_dp/client.py. The vsan_dp package is a dependency-free, standard-library-only Python client for the VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 vSAN Data Protection snapshot appliance (Snapservice). It already routes the four REST operations named in docs/contract.json and authenticates with the vmware-api-session-id session header, but it treats a one-time protection group snapshot as finished the moment the appliance accepts the request.

Creating a protection group snapshot is asynchronous. Snapservice.Clusters.ProtectionGroups.Snapshots_create$Task answers 202 with a bare JSON string task identifier, which means only that the request was accepted, never that the snapshot exists. wait_for_task must poll Snapservice.Tasks_get until the reported status is terminal instead of trusting the first response: PENDING, RUNNING and BLOCKED all mean the appliance is still working, and only SUCCEEDED and FAILED are terminal. A SUCCEEDED task returns its Tasks.Info, whose result property carries the identifier of the new snapshot. A FAILED task must raise TaskFailedError carrying the appliance's failure message taken from the task's error messages. A task that has not reached a terminal status when the poll timeout expires must raise TaskTimeoutError. Successive polls must wait the configured interval apart rather than spinning, and take_snapshot must not read the snapshot back until the task has actually succeeded.

Preserve the exact spec-derived wire shape. An optional request-body property that the caller did not set is omitted from the serialized JSON object rather than encoded as null, zero, an empty string, or an empty object: create_snapshot called without a retention argument must send {"name": ...} with no retention property present at all. The same rule governs optional query parameters. list_protection_groups must leave an unset filter out of the query string entirely rather than sending it blank, and a filter that is set must use form/explode serialisation, repeating the parameter name once per value. The create request must carry the vmw-task=true query parameter and a Content-Type of application/json.

Keep the public API unchanged: SnapshotClient(base_url, session_id, poll_interval=..., poll_timeout=..., timeout=...) exposing list_protection_groups(cluster, pgs=, names=, states=, vms=, cluster_pairs=), create_snapshot(cluster, pg, name, retention=), get_task(task_id), wait_for_task(task_id, interval=, timeout=), get_snapshot(cluster, pg, snapshot) and take_snapshot(cluster, pg, name, retention=, interval=, timeout=); the RetentionPeriod(unit=, duration=) dataclass; and the VsanDpError, ApiError, TaskFailedError and TaskTimeoutError exceptions, all exported from the vsan_dp package. An error response from the appliance must continue to raise ApiError carrying its HTTP status. The interval and timeout arguments of wait_for_task and take_snapshot override the client's poll_interval and poll_timeout when supplied.

Use docs/contract.json as the local source of truth for paths, parameters, schemas and task semantics; it is derived from the vSAN Data Protection OpenAPI specification revision recorded in docs/official_sources.json. Use only the Python standard library. Do not modify docs/contract.json, docs/official_sources.json, or anything under tests/.
